findings.why: Year 50: the 675 cells are the Bactrian south, which the Kangju page makes Yuezhi-ruled ('acknowledges sovereignty to the Yuezhi people in the South') and the Kushan page has the Kushans dividing Bactria in 128 BC, so Kushan keeping them is right. 51-224: the 168-170 Ferghana/Dayuan cells go to Kangju, matching the Kangju page ('gained control of Dayuan and Sogdiana', independent policy to the 3rd century); the Kushan page never names Ferghana/Dayuan (kushan ledger/2 is Cliopatria's reading) and its vague 'Kyrgyzstan' / Shapur I 'Kash, Sughd, Chachestan' (c. 260) sentences do not override that. The size rule gives the page-supported answer.

The 95-96 cells at Bukhara/Navoi/Kashkadarya lie in the Kangju page's Amu Darya-Syr Darya interfluve with Sogdiana; the Parthian Empire page never names Bukhara, Sogdiana, Kangju, Transoxiana or the Amu Darya and puts no city or border near the Oxus/Zeravshan. The Parthian outline there is Cliopatria's reading; the size rule already gives Kangju the land.

Kuninda page: kingdom between the Sutlej and Yamuna 'disappeared around the 3rd century', no mention of the Kushans; Kushan page names no Kuninda or Himalayan foothills. No page has the Kushans ruling the Kunindas and hierarchy.csv has no row, so the size rule (Kuninda keeps its 170 cells) is the page-supported answer.
